purpose: Descriptive actual-pixel audit of the pass-4 bounded concrete-surface and Unreal RFID-contact changes. This is not a perceptual-quality score, an engine ranking, or a model-benefit measurement.

method.reference_scope: Fresh, time-diverse LED RGB and IR/non-LED grayscale frames were opened at actual pixels. IR was used only for stable form, topology and edge evidence, never for color, exposure or roughness fitting.
method.roi_selection: Manual interior surface ROIs were selected after opening the full-resolution images. The real and synthetic views are not geometrically registered and use different cameras, resolution, exposure, sharpening and compression.
method.luminance: Pillow 8-bit grayscale conversion (approximately BT.601 display-referred luma).
method.gradient: Mean absolute one-pixel horizontal and vertical grayscale difference. The edge fraction counts differences of at least 11/255, approximately 0.04.
method.highpass: Mean absolute difference from a 2 px Gaussian-blurred grayscale crop.
method.controlled_comparison: Blender p3/p4 uses camera_door seed 54244 and the same ROI. Unreal r13/r15 uses camera_door seed 58526 and the same ROI. The pass-4 surface/contact implementation is the intended source change; sensor/post-process settings remain fixed within each pair.
method.interpretation_limit: Sensor noise and sharpening inflate gradients, especially in Unreal's post-sensor image. Values expose missing or excessive spatial detail; they do not establish photorealism, engine superiority or YOLO accuracy.

observations: The fresh real cylinder contains dense, irregular dark casting pores and a broad size tail; the real cube contains mold skin, cracks and damaged edges. Clean, pitted, edge-worn and spalled regimes are therefore categorical bounded augmentation, not measured prevalence.

The real cylinder ROI has mean gradient 0.01249, edge fraction 0.05528 and 2 px high-pass 0.01484. Unreal r15's representative cylinder ROI remains lower at 0.00750, 0.00465 and 0.00595 despite post-sensor noise. The geometry proxy does not close the real pore/aggregate gap.

The real cube ROI has edge fraction 0.02820 and 2 px high-pass 0.00776; Blender p4's controlled cube ROI remains 0.00055 and 0.00352. Blender's shader is coherent but still lacks the real sparse high-contrast pore, chip and crack tail.
Blender p3 to p4 changes are modest but widespread: mean absolute RGB difference 0.00995 and high-pass 0.00318 to 0.00352. This is a safe bounded texture increase, not a scan-quality match.

Unreal r13 to r15 changes affect only localized pore geometry: 0.849% of RGB channels changed by more than two levels. Replacing protruding spheres with thin tangent dark discs removed the bead-like cue in inspected pixels; the remaining circular proxy is not a true cavity.

The combined actual-pixel sheet makes the residual domain gap explicit: Unreal still has low-frequency cloudy concrete, coarse cabinet/press geometry and harsh global lighting; Blender remains too smooth and clean at concrete edges.
